C001.reason: SpeedMps field changed from float to double in new schema. Remove explicit (float) cast to preserve input precision through serialization.

C002.reason: entity.SpeedMps is already decoded as double from wire. Dictionary value assignment uses the decoded value directly; no change needed for the speed_mps key.

C003.reason: entity.SpeedMps > 30.0 comparison works identically for double type. The >30 threshold preserved with double precision comparison.

edits.before: var sample = new Simulation.Telemetry.VehicleTelemetry { VehicleId = request.VehicleId, SpeedMps = (float)request.Speed };
edits.after: var sample = new Simulation.Telemetry.VehicleTelemetry { VehicleId = request.VehicleId, SpeedMps = request.Speed };

rationale: The protobuf schema changed speed_mps from float to double. In C#, float is 32-bit and double is 64-bit. The explicit (float) cast was narrowing the double input from the request, losing precision. Removing the cast allows the double value to be assigned directly to SpeedMps, preserving input precision through serialization. The parsed entity.SpeedMps is already decoded as double from the wire format, and the comparison and dictionary operations work correctly with double values. Python float and TypeScript number already support binary64, so cross-language consistency is maintained.
assumptions: Protobuf-generated C# bindings for double field use double type
